items.text: divide, truncating toward zero; 0 when the divisor is 0
power: 1 when the exponent is 0 or less, else the base multiplied by itself exponent minus 1 times
condition, then and else: the then-value when the condition is not 0

items.name: a condition: (lvl < 5) ? lvl : lvl x 3 - par1
a function call with no table: 5, 3, then function 0

text.intro: Type a toy formula as bytes in hex, up to 40, apart by spaces or commas, and the three numbers it may read: variable 0 is lvl, 1 is par1, 2 is par2, and any other variable reads 0. The table runs the evaluator one byte at a time. The bytes and numbers offered first are illustrative; no formula of the game is read.
text.formulaLabel: Formula bytes in hex (typed by hand)

word.callNone: this widget has no function table: pushes 0 and the arguments stay
word.binary: right operand popped, then left; push
word.halt: ends the evaluation: the value is the top of the stack, 0 when it is empty
word.cut: the operand starts at or past the end: the evaluation returns 0
word.trap: the divide of the smallest 32-bit number by -1: by a reading of the code the processor raises a divide error here, so nothing is returned
word.past: the bytes ran out: the evaluation returns 0, whatever is on the stack

text.errBad: A token is not one or two hex digits:
text.errLong: More than 40 bytes were typed; the table shows none.
text.errCut: An operand starts inside the bytes and runs past the last one; the table shows none.
text.note: Computed by our model of the evaluator, not observed in the game. Values are 32-bit integers that wrap; the stack holds 64 values. An operand that starts inside the bytes and runs past the last one is refused: the page does not say what the evaluator reads there. Left out: the compiler that turns formula text into bytes, the contexts and their variables and function tables, and the stock formulas themselves; the bytes are toy bytes typed here, not read from any file.
